reason: Attacked as a hedge and it survives, but it stays a hedge and the note needs one more sentence. What I could establish. The French original is real and is Eberhardt’s: the Bibliotheque nationale de France prints Le droit a l’errance from Pages d’Islam, ed. Victor Barrucand, Fasquelle, Paris, 1932, pp. 279 to 281, and its opening runs Un droit que bien peu d’intellectuels se soucient de revendiquer, c’est le droit a l’errance, au vagabondage. Et pourtant, le vagabondage, c’est l’affranchissement, et la vie le long des routes, c’est la liberte. Rompre un jour bravement toutes les entraves dont la vie moderne et la faiblesse de notre coeur, sous pretexte de liberte, ont change notre geste, s’armer du baton et de la besace symboliques, et s’en aller! Every element of the proposed English answers to that French, sentence for sentence, including the parenthetical about the pretext of liberty and the symbolic stick and bundle, and including the comma after deliverance, which mirrors the comma after affranchissement. So this is a free but faithful translation of a real passage, not a paraphrase minted later and not a misattribution. The named translation is also real and correctly described: the archive.org MARC record for the scanned copy gives The oblivion seekers, and other writings, Eberhardt, Isabelle, 1877 to 1904, San Francisco, City Lights Books, 1975, 88 p., translated by Paul Bowles, so the 1972 date some reviews give is wrong and the source line’s 1975 is right. Two independent secondary witnesses tie this text to Bowles: JSTOR Daily quotes vagrancy is deliverance and life on the open road is the essence of freedom and credits The Oblivion Seekers, and a review of the City Lights book quotes for no one is free who is not alone, the next sentence of the same piece, and names the piece Bowles titled Pencilled Notes. Both sentences sit in the text at The Anarchist Library, which is the wording proposed, so the identification of that text as Bowles is sound on the balance. What I could not establish, and why this is still a hedge. The City Lights page was never seen: the archive.org copy oblivionseekerso0000eber is lending only, its djvu.txt returns 401 and its search-inside endpoint answers Item not available, HathiTrust holds no copy, and the Google Books API is closed to this session. The Anarchist Library page carries no translator credit at all: its stated source is spunk.org, retrieved 2 February 2011, date unknown, so the attribution to Bowles rests on two overlapping phrases and not on a credit line, and rival published translations of Eberhardt exist that could in principle be confused with it, Sharon Bangert’s Prisoner of Dunes and Hamdy and Rice’s Departures among them. The third sentence of the quotation, To have the courage to smash the chains, has no witness at all outside that one page. And JSTOR Daily prints the second sentence without the comma after deliverance, so the two witnesses to the Bowles wording disagree on one mark; the French favours the comma, which is why I would keep it, but the editor should know the witnesses differ. One further caveat the note should carry: Pages d’Islam is a Barrucand compilation, and Barrucand is known to have edited and embellished Eberhardt’s manuscripts, so even the French is Barrucand’s Eberhardt. None of that makes the line false, and nothing here is minted. Other checks all pass. shipped.js: not shipped, nothing near, Eberhardt 0 of 3 in the year, not banned; not on the misattribution list. In scope: a piece by a named author dead in 1904, in a translation published 1975, well before 1999, not scripture, film, lyric, proverb, business or oratory. Publishable, nothing needing a warning. Ends in an exclamation mark. Tag Essay is defensible for a titled reflective prose piece, though a reader who knows Bowles’s book might call Pencilled Notes closer to Diary; Essay is the better fit for the French piece it translates. Source leads with the name, has no dash, no straight double quote, 87 characters, and the piece within the collection is a sufficient locator, with the page number rightly dropped. Fit for Renewal and the Way is the best in the batch after 04-phil-14. Recommendation: ship as a hedge, and add to the note that the witness to Bowles’s wording is an uncredited reprint of spunk.org tied to Bowles by two secondary quotations, not the City Lights page itself.
